headline: Open-book test settles it: MIT's escape lives in the weights, not the words
lede: The WEIGHT SURGERY lab ran its step-4 control (#1580): MIT's written diagnosis, verbatim, fed to the unedited base model at the identical 32K protocol. Reading it changed nothing measurable — the content-vs-weights question the last round left open is settled.

notes.text: #1580 shipped (0b6ebb0): open-book row scored once — MATH 2.0% acc/3.0% fin, GSM8K 4.0/4.0 (MIT-checker agrees: 3.0/4.0). −5.0 pts vs the same-window base control, mean tokens ~31.9K: the diagnosis doesn't even shorten the thinking. 36.5 pts short of the p50cw weights edit; finished 3.5% vs 62.5%.

Verdict: knowledge-transferable content is ruled out at this horizon — the loop escape MIT achieved is not reducible to their write-up. Trust boundary held: final_answer.md was the only MIT artifact read; the row's model claim stays qwen35-base, gated against contamination.
Harness lesson: a verdict must need its control — dropping the same-window base crashed the page verdict on null.toFixed; now it reverts to honest IN FLIGHT instead (mutant-gated). ws3check 119→135.

Board: #1570 held by slot b (robokit 4a draft PR WIP), game-queue's oldest is #838 MYST (item 1 merged), #1572 with QA. Slot-a ws worktrees (step3/4/openbook) may be retired — the .venv chain is no longer load-bearing.
